_comment: Guided tour for the TTTR toolbox. Panel targets against the left navigation list; steps wait for the user to select the row. The organising idea is the two clocks (macro vs micro time), because nearly every mistake in this window is confusing one for the other. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: Two clocks, and nearly every mistake here confuses them
steps.text:
A TTTR file is one record per photon: which detector, when it arrived on the free-running experiment clock (the macro time, ns to hours), and how long after the laser pulse (the micro time, ps, wrapping every pulse period).

Bursts and correlation curves are built from the first. Lifetimes and decays from the second. Hold that apart and this window is straightforward. Seven steps.

steps.title: Start by looking, not by editing
steps.text:
Per-detector count rates across many files at once. This is the cheapest check that exists on a dataset, and it catches the things that later masquerade as analysis problems: a detector that died mid-session, a sample that bleached, a file recorded with the shutter shut.

Run it before you touch anything else.

await.hint: Select Count Rate Analysis on the left.

steps.title: Moving alternation from one clock to the other
steps.text:
ALEX encodes which laser was on in the macro time. PIE pipelines identify the excitation source from the micro time. So ALEX data cannot run through a PIE analysis at all until this conversion is done — and once it is, the same file works with every PIE-based tool in ChiSurf.

It is not a formality; it is a change of which clock carries the information.

steps.title: Detectors do not agree on when zero is
steps.text:
Detectors and their cables have different delays, so two channels of one measurement can have IRFs offset by hundreds of picoseconds. Nothing warns you: the decay looks fine, and the offset lands directly in any lifetime fitted across channels.

Shift here, then go back and look at the IRF. That is the only thing that confirms the shift went the way you intended.

steps.title: Look at the photons before trusting a summary
steps.text:
Every histogram and count rate here is a summary of individual records. When a summary looks wrong, the Photon Table shows the records themselves: routing channel, micro time and macro time, one row per photon, filtered by channel.

Splitting files and editing headers are file-level operations; they live in File tools.

steps.title: One rule, and one oddity
steps.text:
The rule: everything here writes new files — keep the originals. A micro-time shift is not invertible once you have forgotten what it was.

The oddity: the Audifier plays the photon stream as sound. It is not a joke. Bursts, blinking and afterpulsing have distinct signatures by ear, and some artefacts are genuinely easier to notice that way than in a plot.

The ? button has the long version.
